title: spiral-priority-router-for-plan-classes-and-quota-aware-decisioning
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: Implement a 'spiral priority' routing component that assigns incoming requests to region+tier lanes (free, paid, enterprise) with quota-aware admission and deterministic fallback to cheaper model variants. The feature combines admission control, soft demotion windows, and shortest-debt-first scheduling to preserve latency SLOs for paying customers while allowing best-effort servicing for free-tier traffic.

Background & motivation: We currently observe tail latency spikes during regional congestion and quota exhaustion where free-tier traffic either starves paying customers (rare) or causes noisy metrics in aggregated dashboards. Existing tickets improved weighted queues and credit pools but rely on coarse global gating. This task aims to build a compact, testable router that: (1) understands tenant plan class, (2) consults token-credit budgets atomically, (3) routes to region-fallbacks or model-variants (quantized/cheaper), and (4) emits traceable decisions for Console.

Goals:
- Deterministic priority admission per request that respects tenant quota and configurable plan policies.
- Soft demotion behavior: short-term deprioritization windows instead of hard drops to avoid oscillation.
- Built-in fallback to cheaper model variants (e.g., full->quantized or vm-small) when quotas are tight.
- Observable metrics: per-plan admission rate, demotion events, fallback reasons, and added latency/cost delta.
- Rollout capability with canary on Dedicated, fallback to hosted API behavior if misconfigured.

Design proposal:
1) Core components: SpiralPriorityRouter (SPR), PlanQuotaInspector (PQI), DemotionWindowManager (DWM), FallbackSelector (FS).
2) Admission flow per request:
   a) Request enters SPR with metadata (tenant_id, plan_class, model_id, region_hint).
   b) PQI performs an atomic token budget check against tenant and plan pools (fast path: local cache with conservative expiry).
   c) If PQI approves, forward to normal scheduler. Emit admit=true.
   d) If PQI denies due to quota, DWM evaluates whether to soft-demote (assign lower priority lane for X ms) or to immediate fallback to model variant. Decision factors: recent failure rate, latency slack, plan_class weight, and configured grace_level.
   e) FS chooses model_variant based on plan and region (ordered preference list). FS also enforces cost ceiling for free-plan fallbacks.
   f) Record structured decision into trace/span with tags: decision=admit|soft_demote|fallback, reason=quota|region_saturated|latency_spike, chosen_variant, demotion_ttl_ms.

3) Policy config: new 'plan_routing' block in the routing config:
   - tiers: [free, paid, enterprise]
   - tier_weights: {enterprise: 100, paid: 60, free: 10}
   - demotion_policies: {free: {grace_level: 0.4, fallback_variants: [quant-8, small-8]}, paid: {...}}
   - quota_check_mode: strict|soft_cached
   - regional_spill_strategy: prefer-region|nearest-low-cost|global-fanout

Implementation notes: use existing credit vault APIs (ENG-46290 style) but add a light-weight local cache to avoid synchronous KVS hits on p95 path. PQI must return a token_leash object so DWM can decrement or rollback atomically. Integrate with existing admission controller framework so we reuse Prometheus counters and tracing hooks.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strong consistency vs speed: we choose eventual-consistent local cache with periodic reconciliation to keep path latency low while accepting slight overconsumption windows for high-throughput accounts.
- Complexity of demotion windows: keep DWM rules simple (exponential backoff TTLs) to avoid oscillation.
- Cost-complex fallback selection: limit to top-2 cheaper variants to avoid cross-model behavior regressions.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for PQI cache hit/miss semantics, demotion TTL math, and FS ranking logic.
- Integration test harness that replays production request traces (sanitized) to verify admission fairness and that enterprise p95 remains within SLO under synthetic quota exhaustion.
- Chaos test: simulate region outage and verify that regional_spill_strategy preserves enterprise admission while demoting free.
- Load test in dedicated staging with 50k rps mixed plan distribution and validate cost delta and token consumption metrics.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (Canary): Deploy SPR as opt-in routing config for a small subset of internal tenants and run for 2 weeks. Monitor metrics: plan_admit_rate, fallback_rate, plan_p95_latency.
- Phase 2 (Gradual): Expand to 10% of customers on non-critical regions for 48 hours, rollback on >3x fallback_rate baseline.
- Phase 3 (Full): Enable by default for new routing configs; provide a UI toggle in Console for team to switch to legacy admission if needed.

Observability: Add new Console dashboards: Plan Admission Heatmap, Fallbacks by Variant, Demotion TTL distribution, Cost-savings per plan. Create alerts: sustained fallback_rate > 2% for paid/enterprise, sudden spike in soft_demote events.

API/SDK compatibility: Expose decision metadata as response header x-redwood-route-decision (short tags) and as extended trace field via existing tracing headers. SDKs can optionally expose a detailed routing_reason in debug mode.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests pass in CI.
- Canary region results show enterprise p95 unchanged or improved, paid p95 within 5% of baseline, free-tier sufficiently degraded but served (no hard drop).
- Console shows clear explainability per request and alerts configured.
- Engineering runbook updated with rollback steps and troubleshooting checklist.

Documentation & artifacts:
- Link to design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/spiral-priority-router (draft).
- Link to staging PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1891 (WIP).
- Simulation notebook: gs://redwood-storage/routing-sims/spiral-priority-2026-02.ipynb

Notes on uniqueness vs previous tickets: This ticket prioritizes deterministic per-request decisioning with a compact demotion window model and an explicit model-variant fallback selector. Prior tickets leaned on global credit shaping or weighted queues; SPR aims to be a modular router replacement that can be toggled at per-tenant config without wholesale queue redesign.
